punchline: Instant photography started with a three-year-old asking why she couldn't see the picture her father had just taken.
thirty_sec: In 1943, Edwin Land took a photo of his three-year-old daughter on vacation, and she asked why she couldn't see it right away. The obvious answer was that film has to be developed. Land didn't give it. He took her question seriously and started working out how a camera could show the picture immediately. Polaroid's instant camera went on sale in 1948.
